alignments.note: The ASV writes no preposition for the distributive phrase, rendering it Every sabbath day (rule 40).
The ASV writes the quantifying determiner Every where the phrase's the would stand, so the article takes it (rule 41). The competing reading marks the article unrepresented and the Every added.
Second occurrence of the distributive phrase, which the ASV renders once (rule 22).
Finite verb with subject pronoun and auxiliary (rule 17), rendered as the light verb phrase set in order and headed on the complement (rule 44); discontinuous around the object (rule 25).

מֵאֵת rendered by the one compound preposition on the behalf of fuses under rule 30's one-rendering condition, and rule 24 heads it on the content word the phrase turns on, no word here realizing the preposition's own lexeme. The phrase is an adjunct modifying the predicate nominal, not the clause's predicate, so rule 49 does not hand it the construction-supplied copula; that goes to בְּרִית under rule 20. The ASV's marginal Or, from is a competing rendering, not a competing alignment.
Construct noun with the supplied the, the rectum being an anarthrous name (rule 29).

Predicate nominal of the verbless clause, taking the construction-supplied dummy subject and copula it is under rule 20 together with its indefinite article (rule 15); the chain is rendered attributively (rule 28), so no of is placed. The unit is discontinuous around the fronted adjunct phrase under rule 25, exactly as חֻקַּת עוֹלָם takes it shall be at LEV.24.3. The competing reading gives the copula to the מֵאֵת phrase because the English writes it there, which rule 20 forbids: read the Hebrew clause for which side is the predicate rather than the English word order.

review_notes: Corrected: the construction-supplied it is moves from the מֵאֵת unit to בְּרִית, the clause's nominal predicate, bringing this verse into line with LEV.24.3, where the same shape gives it shall be to חֻקַּת. Rule 49 reaches a preposition that is itself the predicate; מֵאֵת בְּנֵי־יִשְׂרָאֵל is an adjunct that the ASV fronts, and rule 20 directs that the Hebrew clause and not the English word order decides which side is the predicate.

The מֵאֵת unit is otherwise unchanged: still one fused compound preposition under rule 30, still headed on behalf under rule 24. Splitting it would leave one of the two morphemes without an English word of its own.
The doubled בְּיוֹם הַשַּׁבָּת is rendered once; rule 22 leaves the second set unrepresented, and rule 41 gives Every to the first article as the determiner written in its place.
